title: Hybrid Reserve + On-Demand Burst SKU: Simplified Enterprise Packaging and Security Q Prep
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Enterprise customers ask for predictable reserved capacity plus the ability to absorb short spikes without complex contract addenda. Current offers (flat reserve + isolated burst credits) create negotiation friction and long security questionnaire cycles when we propose multiple SKUs. Goal: Design a single, easy-to-explain SKU that combines a time-bound reserved baseline with an automated, metered burst band (behaves like on-demand for short windows) and a shrink-wrapped negotiated SLA ladder. The SKU should reduce legal back-and-forth on SOWs and make answers on security questionnaires (SOC/KMS/data isolation) straightforward by limiting variation in network/topology requirements across a contract.
hypothesis: A hybrid Reserve+On-Demand Burst SKU (one contract template, three SLA tiers) will (1) reduce sales cycle time by >=20%, (2) lower legal/security questionnaire follow-up items by >=30%, and (3) increase conversion for mid-market accounts on Dedicated by +12% compared to current reserve-only offers.
acceptance_criteria: Single customer-facing SKU documentation page published in Console docs
One contract template (SOW) drafted and approved by Legal with clear definitions for reserved baseline, burst window, and preemption behavior
Updated security questionnaire answers for top-10Enterprise templates checked into Confluence and reviewed by Security
Implementation acceptance tests from Eng for accurate metered billing during burst windows (end-to-end)
Pilot closed-loop with 3 sales customers signed under the new SKU and usage reconciliation completed
decisions: Adopt time-windowed burst concept: 5-60 minute burst windows with daily cap
Three SLA tiers: Standard (best-effort burst), Gold (guaranteed minimal burst), Platinum (dedicated burst lane with priority routing)
Burst billing model: per-minute meter during burst windows + capped monthly burst allowance for each tier
Security approach: no change to data plane — same VPC model as Dedicated; security Q templates focus on capacity semantics, not new access patterns
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers expect unlimited burst; Mitigation: clear cap language and examples in pricing calculator
Risk: Billing inaccuracies during short bursts; Mitigation: ENG to deliver high-resolution billing events and reconciliation dashboard
Risk: Sales confusion with too many SLA tiers; Mitigation: three-tier max and one-page comparison matrix for AE enablement
